Study: Harrington et al. — When Does Continual Learning Require Learning

Document Scope: Full SEC Form 10-K filings, typically 10,000–13,000 tokens
Prediction or Analysis Target: Direction of the issuer’s 30-day forward simple stock return
Method / Models: Sequential LLM updating via prompting, fine-tuning, reinforcement learning, and context compression/distillation

Defensible Distinction: Disclosure Drift studies the pre-/post-2022 GenAI era, one-year operating outcomes, calibration, style versus evidence model families, and paired rewrites.
Final Novelty Assessment: Precludes first temporal 10-K prediction-drift claim; does not duplicate combined project.

Study: Zhang et al. — Bankruptcy Prediction from 10-K Narratives

Final Novelty Assessment: Precludes first one-year adverse-outcome prediction from 10-K narrative claim.

Study: Blankespoor, deHaan, and Li — Generative AI in Financial Reporting
Sample / Period: U.S. disclosures from 2010–2024; report counts vary by disclosure; linguistic tests contain hundreds of thousands of sentence-level observations
Document Scope: 10-Q/K risk factors and MD&A, prepared call remarks, earnings releases, and IPO filings
Prediction or Analysis Target: Estimated GenAI usage and associated linguistic properties
Method / Models: Validated GPTZero GenScore with synthetic replacement tests and fixed-effects regressions
Primary Metrics: GenScore shifts and regression coefficients for length, readability, tone, and specificity

Defensible Distinction: Disclosure Drift does not infer authorship; it evaluates downstream predictive reliability and evidence-grounded defenses.
Final Novelty Assessment: Precludes first GenAI-in-financial-reporting or disclosure-language-change claim.
